text: Works as a drop-in replacement for Terraform and keeps existing workflows and configurations
quote: It serves as a **drop-in replacement for Terraform**, preserving your existing workflows and configurations.

text: Can be installed through many methods across different operating systems
quote: You can install OpenTofu via a wide range of methods. Please select your operating system and installation method

text: The plan command builds an execution plan so you can preview infrastructure changes before applying them
quote: The `tofu plan` command creates an execution plan, which lets you preview the changes that OpenTofu plans to make to your infrastructure.

text: Speculative plans let developers check the effect of changes before submitting them for code review
quote: developers can use speculative plans to verify the effect of their changes before submitting them for code review

text: Destroy mode creates a plan that removes all existing remote objects, for example to tear down transient dev environments
quote: Destroy mode: creates a plan whose goal is to destroy all remote objects that currently exist, leaving an empty OpenTofu state.

text: Refresh-only mode updates state and outputs to match changes made to remote objects outside OpenTofu
quote: Refresh-only mode: creates a plan whose goal is only to update the OpenTofu state and any root module output values to match changes made to remote objects outside of OpenTofu.

text: The test command creates real infrastructure, checks assertions, then destroys the resources it created
quote: The `tofu test` command lets you test your OpenTofu configuration by creating real infrastructure and checking that the required conditions (assertions) are met. Once the test is complete, OpenTofu destroys the resources it created.

text: Module authors can write separate tests for OpenTofu and for Terraform
quote: useful for module authors who want their modules to support both OpenTofu and Terraform and want to create different tests for each.

text: The import command finds an existing resource by ID and brings it into OpenTofu state at a given address
quote: Import will find the existing resource from ID and import it into your OpenTofu state at the given ADDRESS.

text: Encrypts state and plan files at rest, both locally and in backends
quote: OpenTofu supports encrypting state and plan files at rest, both for local storage and when using a backend.

text: Encryption also works with the terraform_remote_state data source
quote: OpenTofu supports encrypting state and plan files at rest, both for local storage and when using a backend. In addition, you can also use encryption with the `terraform_remote_state` data source.

text: Supports an AES-GCM encryption method for state
quote: Configure AES-GCM encryption method

text: State encryption integrates with AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault and OpenBao key management
quote: If you use a key management system (AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault, or OpenBao), use a separate key for each state file

text: Encryption can be configured in OpenTofu code or through the TF_ENCRYPTION environment variable
quote: You can configure encryption in OpenTofu either by specifying the configuration in the OpenTofu code, or using the `TF_ENCRYPTION` environment variable.

text: The -exclude flag leaves selected resources out of operations, for finer control during testing and rollouts
quote: Selectively exclude resources from operations with the -exclude flag. This provides more control during testing and rollouts, allowing you to focus on specific parts of your infrastructure.

text: Provider configurations can be generated dynamically with for_each for multi-region and multi-environment setups
quote: Dynamically generate provider configurations with for_each, eliminating repetitive code and improving maintainability. Perfect for multi-region deployments, multi-environment setups (dev/staging/prod)...

text: Module versions can be updated programmatically through a single variable for centralized version management
quote: Update all your modules programmatically with a single variable change. Never miss updating a module version by accident - keep your infrastructure consistent and secure with centralized version management.

text: Builds a resource dependency graph and creates or modifies non-dependent resources in parallel
quote: OpenTofu builds a graph of all your resources, and parallelizes the creation and modification of any non-dependent resources.

text: Ecosystem of more than 3,900 providers and 23,600 modules for managing infrastructure on every cloud platform
quote: With a thriving ecosystem of **3,900+ providers** and **23,600+ modules**, you can build and manage infrastructure across every cloud platform with confidence.

text: Defines cloud and on-premises resources in human-readable config files that can be versioned, reused and shared
quote: lets you define both cloud and on-premises resources in human-readable configuration files that you can version, reuse, and share

text: Manages DNS configurations as version-controlled code and deploys them with a single command
quote: Version control your infrastructure with OpenTofu. Track changes, collaborate with your team, and deploy DNS configurations with a single command.

text: Manages repositories, branch protection and team access as code
quote: Create repositories, set up branch protection, and manage team access in code.

text: Plans can be saved to a file with -out and applied later by passing that file to tofu apply
quote: You can use the optional `-out=FILE` option to save the generated plan to a file on disk, which you can later execute by passing the file to `tofu apply` as an extra argument.

text: .tofu files take precedence over .tf files, so a module can support both OpenTofu and Terraform
quote: This ensures that `.tofu` files always take precedence over `.tf` files when both are available. This scenario can be useful for module authors who want their modules to support both OpenTofu and Terraform.

text: Promises backwards compatibility so existing code keeps working for years
quote: Backwards-compatible - so that the existing code can drive value for years to come

text: Linux Foundation project under a widely accepted open-source license that won't suddenly change
quote: Truly open source - under a well-known and widely-accepted license that companies can trust, that won't suddenly change in the future

text: The -json-into flag writes machine-readable JSON output to a file while human-readable logs are still produced
quote: `-json-into=out.json` - Produces the same output as -json, but redirected to a file. This allows for simultaneous capture of both human readable and machine readable logs.

text: An official OCI container image is published on GitHub Container Registry
quote: Use official OCI container image available on GitHub Container Registry.

text: A machine-readable latest.json endpoint publishes nightly build information for automated tooling
quote: For those who want to automate with tooling, `https://nightlies.opentofu.org/nightlies/latest.json` will be kept up to date with the latest build information.
